findings.summary: Idempotence is the property that an operation can be applied multiple times without changing the result beyond the initial application. In computer science, this means repeated calls leave system state unchanged, making operations safe to retry. The concept originates from abstract algebra, where elements or operations satisfy x·x = x, and extends to functions, morphisms, and practical systems like database lookups or address changes that produce identical outcomes regardless of invocation count.

mechanisms.title: Algebraic definition
mechanisms.explanation: An element x of a set S with binary operation · is idempotent if x·x = x. The operation · is idempotent if x·x = x for all x in S. This formal condition underlies all mathematical and computational uses of the property.

mechanisms.title: Computational retry safety
mechanisms.explanation: A subroutine or function is idempotent when multiple calls have the same effect as a single call on system state. This allows operations to be retried without unintended side effects, which is essential for fault tolerance in networked systems.
